title: Schrödinger's Chaos(5x5)
author: PrissyP
rules:
Welcome to Schrödinger's Chaos, a series of 8 puzzles, with two puzzles released each week on Wednesdays and Saturdays!

All puzzles are only 5×5, but don't underestimate them, the logic can still be challenging. Today's puzzle is an easy introduction to the ruleset.

Region building plays a major role in these puzzles, which can make them quite brainbending very quickly. If you ever need a small hint because you get stuck feel free to DM me on Discord(PrissyP0431).
I hope you enjoy solving them as much as I enjoyed creating them!

Good luck, and prepare for some chaos!

Rules

Schrödinger’s Chaos Construction:

Divide the grid into 5 orthogonally connected regions. Every row, column and region contains the digits 1–6 exactly once.

Exactly one cell in each row and each column is a Schrödinger cell (S-cell) containing two different digits. Every S-cell belongs to two regions at once: one of its digits counts for the first region, the other digit for the second region.

Every region contains exactly two S-cells, so each region consists of four normal cells plus one digit from each of its two S-cells.

The value of a normal cell is its digit. The value of an S-cell is the sum of its two digits.

Clues:

Clues:
A number in a cell is its value.

Coloured cells belong to the region of their colour.

Play in SudokuPad
solutionCode: The digits of the region in Row 3, Column 3. Left to right, top to bottom(Only the correct digit of each S-Cell).
